abstract: Merged transistor logic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup> (MTL) also known as multicollector logic (MCL) or integrated injection logic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup> (I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>L), is a very recent development. First announced in October, 1972 this digital circuit technique has made bipolar large-scale integration (LSI) a practical proposition and thus seriously challenged the technologies already active in the LSI arena. abstract: The basic development of the telephone instrument and local transmission system appears to be reaching a limit, and future innovation will be the introduction of additional services for the subscriber. Developments in trunk transmission systems and in the switching system will provide not only additional facilities but a reduction in the cost of the basic service. abstract: Corporate planning has become a widely discussed concept in modern business life and many papers and text books on the subject have been written during the last ten to fifteen years. Numerous definitions have been formulated in an attempt to describe in general terms what is in practice a very difficult and complex process. The problem of definition is further aggravated because organisations differ in their fields of activity, their objectives and in the time-span for their decision making. Simply put, an organisation depends on corporate planning for its continued existence and even survival.

abstract: The steelmaking arc furnace possesses properties which make it an unique industrial load to Supply Authorities. The paper reviews these properties with specific emphasis to matters of furnace and supply system design and associated problems of measurement. The development over the past decade of voltage fluctuation measurement is reviewed together with the current guide lines used by the UK Electricity Supply Authority when connecting arc furnaces. Some views are expressed on the likely nature of arc furnace development with specific reference to the United Kingdom.

articleTitle: Electricity in rail transport on the South African railways
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In the year 1919 the South African Railways came to a crucial point of their development in Natal. With traffic on the main line between the Witwatersrand and Durban having increased to a point of track saturation the Administration ‘figuring the nature of the times deceas'd’ had to ‘prophesy with a near aim of the main chances of things to come’ and decided after receiving the consulting engineers' report to electrify a section of line at 3 kV dc between Glencoe and Pietermaritzburg. This decision was, however, made not without considerable opposition from several quarters who maintained that a bundle of string, wire and shellac' as the electromotor was then irreverently called could never replace the steam engine.

The British Post Office or BPO as it is usually referred to, has always been looked upon in South Africa and throughout the world as a world leader in telecommunications and we in South Africa take a hard look at the BPO before taking any major step. abstract: The paper describes some signal processing techniques at present under development for low bit-rate speech communication systems. A comparison is made between these new methods and those at present in use where an attempt is made to maintain the integrity of the speech wave. The new methods seek to isolate the critically important speech parameters and transmit these for later use in the regeneration of the original acoustical signals. The importance of computers in this form of communications research is stressed.

abstract: The maintenance requirements of power systems throughout the world would appear to be very similar in most respects. In the Republic of South Africa the power system plant is subjected, to a greater or lesser degree, to the same service requirements and environmental conditions as are found on power supply systems in other countries. Thus the maintenance policies and procedures in operation in ESCOM follow general overseas practice.

abstract: In South Africa the mining sector and particularly the gold mines of the Witwatersrand have always been a major consumer of electricity and, in fact, it was as a result of the vigorous policy of electrification adopted by the mining groups that the VFP was formed in 1906. The early history and development of the gold mines is a fascinating story and, for general interest, a brief historical review in this connection is given in the first section of this paper. The remaining sections discuss certain aspects of mining loads and requirements to give a general indication of the points requiring consideration in providing electricity supplies to mines.

abstract: A review is given of logic families developed and used during the past twelve years, of which RTL and DTL are mainly of historical interest, now being nearly completely superseded by TTL. The bipolar technology used in the production of these logic families is discussed in brief detail, as well as the MOS technology, in its various forms, which has led to newer families, notably C-MOS logic, with electrical characteristics superior to TTL in some aspects. Present trends in both technologies seem to indicate that the promising silicon-on-sapphire C-MOS development program will be overshadowed by the production of a new bipolar logic, multi-collector logic (MCL), which is inherently suitable for high-density LSI digital circuits. In conclusion, some consideration is given to the influence of all the various factors on the local manufacture of custom-made digital ICs.

articleTitle: An advanced airborne thermal infrared linescanner
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The recording of the thermal properties of objects by optical remote sensing is based on the fact that surfaces at natural environmental temperatures emit radiation predominantly at infrared wavelengths. In consequence, airborne thermal infrared reconnaissance is concerned with the 3 μm to 30 μ m region of the spectrum to measure thermal characteristics in a ground (or water) scene. Since practical photographic emulsions are not sensitive at these wavelengths, solid state devices are needed to detect the emitted radiation. An efficient way of producing a thermal image of the scene over which an aircraft passes is to use a scanning radiometer or linescanner. This paper describes some concepts involved in designing a high performance linescanner. Particular reference is made to the design considerations of a custom-made linescanner<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(21)</sup> capable of recording multispectral thermal imagery with high thermal and spatial resolution. Use of this instrument in a geological application is also described and an example of thermal imagery presented. 10 Summary The concepts involved in the recording of the emitted IR radiation from a ground scene as imaged by an advanced IR line scanner operated from an aircraft have been described. In particular the RS-25 IR line scanner manufactured by Texas Instruments is discussed and a detailed breakdown of its optical and electronic design features is given. These non-standard features were incorporated in order to recover IR imagery of the same spatial and radiometric fidelity maintained by the high performance detector system and scan optics. The RS-25 described is presently a unique system, custom-made for the purpose of geological exploration in Southern Africa. An example of a geological application is given in which thermal differences within a geological sequence were recorded. From these differences geological structure not apparent in conventional photography could be identified.

articleTitle: Some protection, underfrequency load shedding and testing aspects of the ESCOM network
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The power supply system of the Republic, as shown in Fig 1.1 consists of the major load and generation centres in the Transvaal with tight interconnection and relatively short lines. Other important load and generation centres are connected to this area by relatively long transmission lines. There are also a number of smaller load areas with little local generation, importing a relatively large proportion of their load from the Transvaal. The long transmission distances and resulting high capital cost of transmission favour single line supplies, at least in the initial development stages. The long transmission distances also make series compensation economically attractive. The large local loads compared with available generation in the outlying areas necessitate underfrequency load shedding. The paper outlines the approach adopted to these problems in the Republic. South Africa has a high lightning incidence (isoceraunic level over 60) and cane and grass fires are prevalent in the dry season. The resulting faults are predominantly single-phase to ground flashovers at the higher voltages (85 per cent of 400 kV and about 60 per cent of 132 kV faults involve only one phase). The high fault incidence coupled with long transmission distances over single lines makes single-phase auto-reclosing an obvious design feature. It is employed on interconnectors and on radial load systems.

articleTitle: Modern computational tools aid power system planning and operation twenty-fourth bernard price memorial lecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Electric energy is playing a role of increasing importance in each nation's total energy supply. Energy utilization within the USA and the factors leading to the growing participation of electric energy are reviewed. The critical driving forces of increased capital costs, financial and environmental restraints, increasing fuel costs, and regulatory delays lead to the need for more comprehensive understanding of electric power systems. This paper describes modern computational and anafytical techniques that significantly aid the planning, design, and operation of electric power systems.
